## 3. Data Import and Cleaning

```{r load-libraries}
# Load all required packages
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(caret)
library(e1071)
library(pheatmap)
library(pROC)
library(corrplot)
library(randomForest)
```

#{r import-data}
# Load the dataset
df <- read.csv("C:/Users/ADMIN/Documents/Bioinformatic-Project---2020-ASP-83/Data/heart.csv")

# Check size
dim(df)

# Check for missing values
sum(is.na(df))

# Convert categorical variables to factors
df$sex <- factor(df$sex, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("Female", "Male"))
df$cp <- factor(df$cp, levels = c(0,1,2,3), labels = c("Typical Angina", "Atypical Angina", "Non-anginal", "Asymptomatic"))
df$fbs <- factor(df$fbs, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
df$restecg <- factor(df$restecg, levels = c(0,1,2), labels = c("Normal", "Abnormal", "Hypertrophy"))
df$exang <- factor(df$exang, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
df$target <- factor(df$target, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No Disease", "Heart Disease"))

# Check cleaned data
str(df)


## 4. Exploratory Data Analysis

#{r eda-plot1}
# Figure 1 - Age distribution by heart disease outcome
plot1 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = age, fill = target)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 1: Age Distribution by Heart Disease Status",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Number of Patients",
    fill = "Diagnosis"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(plot1)
ggsave("Output/figure1_age_distribution.png", plot1, width = 8, height = 5)


#{r eda-plot2}
# Figure 2 - Chest pain type by heart disease outcome
plot2 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = cp, fill = target)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge", color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 2: Chest Pain Type by Heart Disease Status",
    x = "Chest Pain Type",
    y = "Number of Patients",
    fill = "Diagnosis"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))

print(plot2)
ggsave("Output/figure2_chest_pain.png", plot2, width = 8, height = 5)


#{r eda-plot3}
# Figure 3 - Boxplots of cholesterol and max heart rate by outcome
plot3 <- df %>%
  select(target, chol, thalach) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(chol, thalach), 
               names_to = "Variable", 
               values_to = "Value") %>%
  mutate(Variable = recode(Variable,
    "chol" = "Cholesterol (mg/dl)",
    "thalach" = "Max Heart Rate (bpm)")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = target, y = Value, fill = target)) +
  geom_boxplot(color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~Variable, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 3: Cholesterol and Max Heart Rate by Heart Disease Status",
    x = "Diagnosis",
    y = "Value",
    fill = "Diagnosis"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

print(plot3)
ggsave("Output/figure3_boxplots.png", plot3, width = 8, height = 5)


#{r eda-heatmap}
# Figure 4 - Correlation heatmap of clinical features
library(pheatmap)

# Select numeric columns and calculate correlation
numeric_df <- df %>%
  select(age, trestbps, chol, thalach, oldpeak, ca) %>%

# Save heatmap
png("Output/figure4_heatmap.png", width = 800, height = 600)
pheatmap(numeric_df,

         color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50),
         display_numbers = TRUE,
         number_format = "%.2f",
         fontsize = 12)
dev.off()

# Display heatmap
pheatmap(numeric_df,
         main = "Figure 4: Correlation Heatmap of Clinical Features",
         color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50),
         display_numbers = TRUE,
         number_format = "%.2f",
         fontsize = 12)


## 5. Statistical Tests

#{r stats-tests}
# T-tests for continuous variables
t_age <- t.test(age ~ target, data = df)
t_chol <- t.test(chol ~ target, data = df)
t_thalach <- t.test(thalach ~ target, data = df)
t_trestbps <- t.test(trestbps ~ target, data = df)

# Print t-test results
cat("=== T-TEST RESULTS ===\n")
cat("\nAge p-value:", round(t_age$p.value, 4))
cat("\nCholesterol p-value:", round(t_chol$p.value, 4))
cat("\nMax Heart Rate p-value:", round(t_thalach$p.value, 4))
cat("\nBlood Pressure p-value:", round(t_trestbps$p.value, 4))

# Chi-squared tests for categorical variables
chi_sex <- chisq.test(table(df$sex, df$target))
chi_cp <- chisq.test(table(df$cp, df$target))
chi_exang <- chisq.test(table(df$exang, df$target))

# Print chi-squared results
cat("\n\n=== CHI-SQUARED TEST RESULTS ===\n")
cat("\nSex p-value:", round(chi_sex$p.value, 6))
cat("\nChest Pain p-value:", round(chi_cp$p.value, 6))
cat("\nExercise Angina p-value:", round(chi_exang$p.value, 6))


## 6. Machine Learning Models

#{r train-test-split}
# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Fix factor level names
df$target <- factor(df$target, 
                    levels = c("No Disease", "Heart Disease"),
                    labels = c("NoDisease", "HeartDisease"))

# Split data 80% train, 20% test
trainIndex <- createDataPartition(df$target, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- df[trainIndex, ]
test_data <- df[-trainIndex, ]

cat("Training set rows:", nrow(train_data))
cat("\nTest set rows:", nrow(test_data))


#{r logistic-regression}
# Logistic Regression model with 5-fold cross validation
set.seed(123)

log_model <- train(target ~ .,
                   data = train_data,
                   method = "glm",
                   family = "binomial",
                   trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", 
                                          number = 5,
                                          classProbs = TRUE))

# Test predictions
log_pred <- predict(log_model, test_data)

# Confusion matrix
log_cm <- confusionMatrix(log_pred, test_data$target)
print(log_cm)


#{r random-forest}
# Random Forest model with 5-fold cross validation
set.seed(123)

rf_model <- train(target ~ .,
                  data = train_data,
                  method = "rf",
                  trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", 
                                         number = 5,
                                         classProbs = TRUE))

# Test predictions
rf_pred <- predict(rf_model, test_data)

# Confusion matrix
rf_cm <- confusionMatrix(rf_pred, test_data$target)
print(rf_cm)


#{r svm-model}
# SVM model using e1071
library(e1071)

set.seed(123)

svm_model <- svm(target ~ ., 
                 data = train_data, 
                 kernel = "radial",
                 probability = TRUE)

# Test predictions
svm_pred <- predict(svm_model, test_data)

# Confusion matrix
svm_cm <- confusionMatrix(svm_pred, test_data$target)
print(svm_cm)


#{r roc-curves}
# ROC curves for all models
library(pROC)

# Get probabilities
log_prob <- predict(log_model, test_data, type = "prob")[,2]
rf_prob <- predict(rf_model, test_data, type = "prob")[,2]
svm_prob_raw <- predict(svm_model, test_data, probability = TRUE)
svm_prob <- attr(svm_prob_raw, "probabilities")[,2]

# Create ROC curves
roc_log <- roc(test_data$target, log_prob)
roc_rf <- roc(test_data$target, rf_prob)
roc_svm <- roc(test_data$target, svm_prob)

# Print AUC values
cat("Logistic Regression AUC:", round(auc(roc_log), 4))
cat("\nRandom Forest AUC:", round(auc(roc_rf), 4))
cat("\nSVM AUC:", round(auc(roc_svm), 4))

# Save ROC plot
png("Output/figure5_roc_curves.png", width = 1200, height = 900, res = 150)
plot(roc_log, col = "blue", lwd = 2, 
     main = "Figure 5: ROC Curves for All Models")
plot(roc_rf, col = "red", lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
plot(roc_svm, col = "green", lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
legend("bottomright", 
       legend = c(
         paste("Logistic Regression AUC =", round(auc(roc_log), 3)),
         paste("Random Forest AUC =", round(auc(roc_rf), 3)),
         paste("SVM AUC =", round(auc(roc_svm), 3))),
       col = c("blue", "red", "green"), 
       lwd = 2)
dev.off()

# Display in RStudio
plot(roc_log, col = "blue", lwd = 2, 
     main = "Figure 5: ROC Curves for All Models")
plot(roc_rf, col = "red", lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
plot(roc_svm, col = "green", lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
legend("bottomright", 
       legend = c(
         paste("Logistic Regression AUC =", round(auc(roc_log), 3)),
         paste("Random Forest AUC =", round(auc(roc_rf), 3)),
         paste("SVM AUC =", round(auc(roc_svm), 3))),
       col = c("blue", "red", "green"), 
       lwd = 2)

#{r feature-importance}
# Feature Importance from Random Forest
importance_data <- varImp(rf_model)$importance
importance_data$Feature <- rownames(importance_data)
importance_data <- importance_data[order(importance_data$Overall, 
                                         decreasing = TRUE),]

# Plot feature importance
plot6 <- ggplot(importance_data, 
                aes(x = reorder(Feature, Overall), y = Overall)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "#66B2FF", color = "black") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 6: Feature Importance from Random Forest",
    x = "Clinical Feature",
    y = "Importance Score"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(plot6)
ggsave("Output/figure6_feature_importance.png", plot6, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)

#{r clustering}
# K-means clustering
set.seed(123)

# Select numeric columns for clustering
cluster_data <- df[, c("age", "trestbps", "chol", "thalach", "oldpeak", "ca")]

# Scale the data
scaled_data <- scale(cluster_data)

# K-means with 2 clusters
km <- kmeans(scaled_data, centers = 2, nstart = 25)

# Add cluster to dataframe
df$cluster <- factor(km$cluster)

# Plot using age vs thalach
plot7 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = age, y = thalach, 
                         color = cluster, 
                         shape = target)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("1" = "#FF9999", "2" = "#66B2FF")) +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 7: K-means Clustering of Patients",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Max Heart Rate (bpm)",
    color = "Cluster",
    shape = "Diagnosis"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(plot7)
ggsave("Output/figure7_clustering.png", plot7, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
